{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZcUkGg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDDjLA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 87, "title": "Add durable local NetNews posting and followup journeys", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `029670ce459e02ac0d7af9cb6584ef12ca513cc1`, NetNews supports reading and Subject/From searching across six bundled articles, but users cannot contribute a new article or followup. `src/navigation.ts:handleNetNews` has no contribution path; `src/commands.ts` directs WRITE/REPLY toward other services, and `tests/netnews.spec.ts` explicitly expects their rejection.

This extends the intentionally bounded, completed [reading increment #81](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/81). It is an existing capability gap, not a demonstrated regression from the latest conference change. Contemporary 1996 evidence supports PC-VAN NetNews posting, so the missing participation journey materially limits the recreation.

## Expected outcome

Enable both browser-local keyboard journeys in the two existing example groups:

- Group → WRITE → compose → review/edit → explicit submission → LIST/READ/search the saved article.
- Article → REPLY number → compose a public followup → review → explicit submission → reread with correct References.

Use WRITE and REPLY as discoverable reconstructed product controls. The UI should describe the result as an article/followup, distinguish it from private mail, and identify the destination group during composition and review. Contributions stay in the user's browser; they are never delivered to Usenet.

Keep anonymous reading and all six bundled examples. Human posting uses the existing local handle registration, without AI consent, inference, credentials or external connections.

## Context

Historical sources were inspected live on 2026-10-24:

- [Internet White Paper 1996, comparison labeled January 1996](https://iwparchives.jp/files/pdf/iwp1996/iwp1996-ch04-01-p110.pdf) reports PC-VAN NetNews reading and posting. Confidence is moderate to high for the reported capability. It supplies neither activation dates nor terminal commands. PDF text/table extraction was inspected; no usable page-image comparison was established.
- [Internet Magazine, April 1995, printed page 105](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199504-104-bbs.pdf) documents an earlier read-only PC-VAN service with header searching. Confidence is high within that earlier snapshot. Its restriction must not override the later capability report; neighboring providers' illustrated menus remain separate evidence.
- [April 1996 fj guide appendix](https://www2.biglobe.ne.jp/~nir/misc/fj-no-arukikata/6.1.html) distinguishes posting, followups, cancellation, crossposting and Message-ID versus group-local article numbers. This is contemporary participant guidance, not a PC-VAN session or proof of its controls.
- [Preserved glossary dated November 2, 1996](https://ie.u-ryukyu.ac.jp/~kono/fj/fj.beginners/318.html) distinguishes public followups and the Newsgroups, From, Subject, Message-ID, References and Followup-To fields. Confidence is high in the displayed period concepts; PC-VAN carriage and rendering remain unverified. Reuse no archived identities or prose.
- [RFC 1036, December 1987, sections 2.1.5 and 2.2.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1036.html) documents distinct article identities and followups retaining earlier References followed by the immediate parent's Message-ID, with a Re: subject default. This is strong evidence for period Usenet interchange semantics, not PC-VAN command syntax or a requirement to implement a network protocol.
- A [preserved October 22, 1996 contribution](https://ie.u-ryukyu.ac.jp/~kono/fj/fj.beginners/70.html) remains **snippet-only**: indexed headers include References, a PC-VAN posting host and PC-VAN INETNEWS identification. Direct opening failed. Treat it as limited corroboration, not the basis for exact controls or client-versus-host attribution. Accessible glossary, guide and RFC material supplied alternatives.

Judgment: participation and followup relationships are sufficiently supported for implementation. Exact host prompts, commands, editor behavior, numbering, group carriage, local persistence and return behavior remain category D reconstruction. Continue the existing illustrative carriage of `fj.questions.fj` and `fj.news.usage`; do not claim a complete historical directory. The 1995 restriction does not establish late-1996 behavior.

Implementation findings:

- `src/netnews.ts` contains immutable bundled examples and pure render/search functions. Merge validated local contributions into the selected group's view while keeping bundled content outside backups.
- `src/navigation.ts` holds group/filter/detail context. `src/commands.ts`, `src/connection.ts` and `src/main.ts` need narrowly scoped context/refresh wiring so NetNews composition cannot fall through into forum, conference or mail operations.
- `TerminalComposer` already preserves literal lines, review/edit/cancel behavior, explicit confirmation and failed-save drafts. Reuse it with the smallest necessary presentation extension.
- `createConferenceContribution` demonstrates atomic allocation and idempotent retry using a draft ID. Existing validated settings, backup replacement, world fencing and reset behavior provide a suitable persistence precedent without a new storage framework or object store.
- `tests/netnews.spec.ts`, `tests/conference-repository.spec.ts`, `tests/composition.spec.ts` and terminal helpers supply relevant existing validation patterns. Replace only obsolete NetNews rejection expectations; retain invalid-command and service-isolation coverage.

Live repository-scoped searches returned no open Issues or PRs. NetNews history returned #81 and related wire-news/mail work without an equivalent pending increment. Inventory can change and lexical history searches are incomplete.

[PR #86](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/86) and `docs/validation.md` report 290 passing checks, configured TypeScript checking/build and production conference journeys, including disclosure and correction of an initial fixture failure. Those are Coordinator records for existing behavior, not validation of this proposal. This research graph ran no application, builds, tests or inference and changed no files or external records.

Scope excludes additional groups, remote delivery, arbitrary headers, attachments, crossposting, moderation, Followup-To routing, cancellation of published articles, subscriptions/unread tracking, expiry, thread-navigation systems, AI participation and other Internet services. These remain omitted capabilities rather than claims about historical absence.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] In an existing NetNews group list or article view, WRITE starts a new article and REPLY number starts a public followup to an article in the active results. Reject malformed, unsafe, missing or unavailable targets without changing the current view or records. Directory-level commands remain contextual. Pin the selected group, author and parent identity when starting the draft; decline/cancel registration without creating an article.
- [ ] Reuse the established composer limits and behavior: literal Japanese, internal/leading/trailing whitespace and blank lines; `.TEXT` for command-like text; `.END`; review/edit; explicit Y submission; N/CANCEL discard. BACK/MAIN during a draft preserve it and explain its ownership. Review identifies the group and, for followups, the parent article. Settings access and IME guards cannot accidentally submit or redirect the draft. Draft contents stay out of command history under existing rules.
- [ ] Saved articles expose Newsgroups, From, Subject, Date and Message-ID. Use a fictional `.invalid` address tied consistently to the selected local author; reuse existing stable identity/safe-name conventions without changing their algorithm or exposing raw member keys. No real email address is requested. Record the synthetic address and display policy as reconstruction.
- [ ] A new article has no References. A followup defaults to one Re: prefix and carries its parent's existing reference sequence followed by the parent's Message-ID. Editing Subject does not silently detach the chosen parent. Support replies to bundled originals, bundled followups and saved local followups; demonstrate a multi-generation chain. Equal subjects or equal group-local numbers in different groups never imply a relationship.
- [ ] Keep the six bundled articles and their authored dates unchanged. Persist only local contributions and necessary allocation/reference metadata in a validated, optional service-specific setting or equivalently small existing-storage design. Missing state in older backups means no local contributions. Reading never initializes persistent NetNews state or repopulates restored empty community collections.
- [ ] Allocate stable group-local numbers above the bundled range, initially 4 in each existing group. Message-IDs are stable and unique across both groups and distinct from bundled IDs. Allocate and save atomically; concurrent repository connections cannot duplicate numbers. Repeating the same committed draft returns its original result; conflicting reuse fails. A quota/validation failure leaves no partial article or consumed allocation and permits safe editing/retry. A refresh failure after commit must not leave a sendable duplicate draft.
- [ ] Validate local state on direct writes and JSON restore: known group, valid bounded text/timestamps/provenance, valid human authors, unique identities/numbers, consistent counters and valid earlier same-group parents/reference chains. Resolve bundled parents by Message-ID as well as local parents. Reject dangling, cyclic, future or cross-group relationships and malformed state before replacement. Preserve member-reference safeguards where author references are stored. Rejected/quota-failed restore leaves the existing world intact.
- [ ] Store operational creation timestamps and apply the existing durable historical-calendar projection for local Date presentation, with an appropriate documented NetNews format. Do not rewrite operational timestamps, re-anchor the calendar on reads or dynamically redate bundled examples. Reload and export/import preserve local identities, dates, numbering, attribution and reference relationships.
- [ ] Successful submission clears the active filter and exposes the selected group's complete list, making the saved article immediately readable/searchable. Cancellation leaves the prior view/filter intact. Existing Subject/From literal matching, counts, stable numbers and active-result READ restrictions apply to bundled plus local articles. Preserve HELP, LIST, BACK, MAIN, direct/index parents, repeated navigation and Settings/About return context. Refresh local content before relevant reads so another connection's committed articles become visible.
- [ ] Factory reset removes local NetNews contributions while retaining bundled examples. Import/reset invalidates open drafts through existing world-replacement fences, including stale repository connections. Browsing and cancelled/failed drafts do not alter unrelated world records; successful posting changes only NetNews state, with existing registration and session/history bookkeeping allowed. Preserve forum/mail/conference/OLT records, read markers, consent, AI schedules and calendar settings. NetNews content must not enter resident inference contexts.
- [ ] Add focused tests using existing Playwright/controller/repository tooling for both groups, new posts and multi-generation followups, invalid targets, filtering, concurrent/idempotent saves, failed-save retry, backup compatibility/roundtrip/rejection, reset and stale drafts. Include production keyboard journeys for registration/decline, review/edit/cancel, successful rereading/searching, reload/restore, literal headers/body/log output, IME Enter protection and usable input/scrolling at 320px. Pause automatic activity for protected-record comparisons; observe no external requests or model loading.
- [ ] Update README, research, Settings/About and affected storage/reset disclosures. Record source URLs, inspection dates, historical scope, confidence, snippet/access failures and reconstruction choices. Replace obsolete bundled-only/posting-excluded descriptions without adding repeated provenance notices to normal service output. Preserve existing functional, storage, consent, composition/IME, calendar and terminal pacing/skip coverage.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test` before merge; its existing Playwright configuration already runs TypeScript checking and production build. Use deterministic fixtures/stubs and existing tools, with no new framework or real-model execution. Review the complete diff, affected links and `git diff --check`, and record actual results and any failures accurately.

## Optional validation

Compare controls or layout with a subsequently recovered dated PC-VAN NetNews manual/session. Additional Japanese readability or native-IME review may help but is not a human, hardware or subjective completion gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks can be completed against local production assets before merge.
